documentation: This document outlines the backend architecture, data models (entities), and Firestore database structure for the Advisory Insights Platform. It is designed to ensure data integrity, security, and scalability.

ExperimentMeta.description: Stores immutable metadata about an experiment run, such as the random seed, stimuli versions, and code versions. This is critical for reproducibility.

Participant.description: Represents a single participant in the experiment. All other participant-specific data is nested under this entity.

Response.description: Stores a single answer to a specific question from a participant.

fields.value: string (the answer, potentially encrypted if PII)

DerivedComposite.description: Stores a calculated score (e.g., a mean score for a Likert scale) derived from multiple 'Response' documents.

fields.name: string (name of the composite, e.g., 'DQ_SUB_MEAN')
fields.itemsUsed: array of strings (references to Response IDs used)

DataQualityFlag.description: Flags potential data quality issues for a participant's session.

fields.id: string (unique ID for the flag entry)

firestoreStructure.philosophy: The structure uses a hierarchical model with participant-owned data paths to enable strict security rules. This avoids the need for cross-document 'get()' calls in security rules, which is a best practice.

paths.description: The main collection for participant documents.
Sub-collection for all individual answers from a participant.
Sub-collection for calculated scores for a participant.
Sub-collection for data quality flags for a participant.
